subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native generic provider/auth quota-bucket contract for Gemini project/account quota failures, and should that live in core auth/failover or a provider/plugin-owned seam?
rationale: The choice affects public config/state shape, fallback semantics, status/docs, and the core-versus-provider ownership boundary, which automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Add generic quota buckets
options.body: Introduce additive provider/auth bucket metadata and cooldown semantics while preserving today’s flat rotation behavior as the default.

options.title: Fold into broader pool routing
options.body: Make the broader provider-profile pool routing tracker explicitly own Gemini project/account quota buckets before implementing this slice.

options.title: Keep outside core
options.body: Require provider plugins or sidecars to handle project-aware suppression if maintainers decide current seams are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Add generic quota buckets
recommendation.body: Introduce additive provider/auth bucket metadata and cooldown semantics while preserving today’s flat rotation behavior as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest history match for generic key rotation and adjacent auth-provider failover decisions.
